--- TLS.md ---
LAN HTTP (no TLS) | TLS (https) > Enable HTTP/2 on your reverse proxy
Whichever reverse proxy you use, make sure it serves SilverBullet over HTTP/2. Over HTTP/1.1, browsers allow only six simultaneous connections per host, and SilverBullet’s service worker and sync engine can use all of them. When that happens, every request stalls: the client reports “Could not reach remote server, we’re offline or the server is down”, requests to `/.ping` time out, and pages load slowly from the local copy, even though the server itself is up.

* **Caddy** enables HTTP/2 by default, so the configuration above needs no changes.
* **nginx**: add `http2 on;` to the `server` block (nginx 1.25.1 and later), or use `listen 443 ssl http2;` on older versions.
* **Nginx Proxy Manager**: edit the proxy host, open the _SSL_ tab and enable _HTTP/2 Support_.

--- TLS.md ---
LAN HTTP (no TLS) | localhost (http)
If you run SilverBullet _locally_ on your machine, this is the easiest option. Everything runs fine as long as the browser sees `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` appear in the URL, even with `http://`.

The obvious drawback of this approach is that your SilverBullet instance is _only accessible from the machine you run it on_.

--- Install/Server.md ---
Run Server on this computer | Self-hosted server
You can self host SilverBullet on essentially any Intel-compatible 64-bit or ARM 64-bit machine you have terminal access to. The server needs very limited resources (a few hundred megabytes of RAM is sufficient), so even a Raspberry Pi works.

There are three things to take care of, in this order:

1. Install SilverBullet:
   * [[Install/Server Binary]] — a single self-contained binary
   * [[Install/Docker]] — a docker container
2. Deploy a [[TLS]] layer in front of SilverBullet for encrypted connections and the full feature set. Plain LAN `http://` also works (mostly) but only in online-only mode, see [[TLS#LAN HTTP (no TLS)]] for limitations.
3. Follow [[Getting Started]] to learn the basics of using SilverBullet itself.

CHANGELOG | Edge > 2.11.0
* **LAN HTTP support:** open SilverBullet via a LAN IP or hostname without TLS in online-only mode, with compatible hashing and text copying. Failed loads now preserve the current editor and page list instead of presenting empty content, direct requests update the connection indicator, and the browser warns before leaving an unsaved editor. See [[TLS]] for limitations.
* Fix: a linked-mention snippet that contained a `![[transclusion]]` inlined the entire target page into the Linked Mentions widget -- frontmatter first, rendered as garbage. Snippets now show such a mention as a plain link, and a transcluded page’s frontmatter no longer leaks into rendered widget content. (Triggers a full space reindex on upgrade.)
